24 * A canonical telephone is exactly {@link #REQUIRED_DIGITS} digits with every separator, 25 * prefix or other non-digit character removed, so numbers that differ only in formatting 26 * are stored and compared identically. 27 */ 28 @Component 29 public class TelephoneNormalizer { 30 31 /** The exact number of digits a normalized telephone must contain. */ 32 public static final int REQUIRED_DIGITS = 10; 33 34 /** 35 * Strips every non-digit character from {@code raw}, keeping only its digits. 36 * 37 * @param raw the telephone as supplied by the client, possibly {@code null} 38 * @return the digits contained in {@code raw}; empty when {@code raw} is {@code null} 39 * or holds no digits 40 */ 41 public String normalize(String raw) { 42 return raw == null ? "" : raw.replaceAll("\\D", ""); 43 } 44 45 /** 46 * @param digits an already-normalized telephone 47 * @return {@code true} when it consists of exactly {@link #REQUIRED_DIGITS} digits 48 */ 49 public boolean hasRequiredLength(String digits) { 50 return digits != null && digits.length() == REQUIRED_DIGITS; 51 } 52 } 53

---PROPS---
# active profiles config
#
# the application uses two active profiles
#
# one - for select database
# ------------------------------------------------
# When using HSQL, use: hsqldb
# When using MySQL, use: mysql
# When using PostgreSQL, use: postgres
# When using H2, use: h2
# ------------------------------------------------
#
# and one for selected repository layer
# ------------------------------------------------
# When using Spring jpa, use: jpa
# When using Spring JDBC, use: jdbc
# When using Spring Data JPA, use: spring-data-jpa
# ------------------------------------------------

spring.profiles.active=h2,spring-data-jpa

# ------------------------------------------------

server.port=9966
server.servlet.context-path=/petclinic/

# Default database platform; can be overridden by other profile-specific property sources 
spring.sql.init.platform=h2
# Ensures schema & data reload on every restart (good for local dev)
spring.sql.init.mode=always
spring.sql.init.schema-locations=classpath*:db/${spring.sql.init.platform}/schema.sql
spring.sql.init.data-locations=classpath*:db/${spring.sql.init.platform}/data.sql

spring.messages.basename=messages/messages
spring.jpa.open-in-view=false

# OpenAPI/Swagger UI (Defaults to true)
#springdoc.api-docs.enabled=true
#springdoc.swagger-ui.enabled=true

logging.level.org.springframework=INFO
#logging.level.org.springframework=DEBUG

#logging.level.org.hibernate.SQL=DEBUG
#logging.level.org.hibernate.type.descriptor.sql.BasicBinder=TRACE

# enable the desired authentication type
# by default, the authentication is disabled
petclinic.security.enable=false

---
# H2 Database Configuration
spring.sql.init.platform=h2
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:petclinic;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1;DB_CLOSE_ON_EXIT=FALSE
spring.datasource.driverClassName=org.h2.Driver
spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.password=

# Hibernate Configuration
spring.jpa.database-platform=org.hibernate.dialect.H2Dialect
# Change to 'validate' in production
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
spring.jpa.show-sql=true

# H2 Console Configuration
spring.h2.console.enabled=true
spring.h2.console.path=/h2-console
# HSQLDB config start
#----------------------------------------------------------------
spring.sql.init.platform=hsqldb
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:hsqldb:mem:petclinic
spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.password=
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=none
#----------------------------------------------------------------
# HSQLDB config end
# database init, supports mysql too
spring.sql.init.platform=mysql
spring.datasource.url=${MYSQL_URL:jdbc:mysql://localhost/petclinic}
spring.datasource.username=${MYSQL_USER:petclinic}
spring.datasource.password=${MYSQL_PASS:petclinic}
# SQL is written to be idempotent so this is safe
spring.sql.init.mode=always
spring.sql.init.platform=postgres
spring.datasource.url=${POSTGRES_URL:jdbc:postgresql://localhost/petclinic}
spring.datasource.username=${POSTGRES_USER:petclinic}
spring.datasource.password=${POSTGRES_PASS:petclinic}
# SQL is written to be idempotent so this is safe
spring.sql.init.mode=always

## Summary

I implemented the rule that creating an owner whose normalized telephone is already in use by another owner is rejected with **409 Conflict**, layering the logic where it belongs:

1. **`OwnerRepository`** — declared `boolean existsByTelephone(String telephone)`, a Spring Data–style query method.

2. **Repository implementations** — since telephones are stored in normalized form (the existing `OwnerFieldsValidator` normalizes the DTO to 10 bare digits before the request reaches the controller), the check is a straight equality lookup:
   - `SpringDataOwnerRepository` (active `spring-data-jpa` profile) derives the query automatically from the inherited method name.
   - `JpaOwnerRepositoryImpl` and `JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl` got explicit `COUNT(*)` implementations, keeping all three profiles compiling and consistent.

3. **`ClinicService` / `ClinicServiceImpl`** — added `ownerExistsWithTelephone(...)`, a read-only transactional facade method delegating to the repository, matching the surrounding style.

4. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — before saving, it checks the (already-normalized) telephone via the service and returns `HttpStatus.CONFLICT` if a duplicate exists. This keeps the create-only business rule in the create path (updates are unaffected, so an owner keeping its own number never falsely conflicts).

Both acceptance tests (`coreRejectsDuplicateTelephone`, `functionalityAllowsDistinctTelephone`) and the full suite pass: `BUILD SUCCESS`.
